NDT training in Longview, TX: how it works

Short answer: From Longview you study each method's theory self-paced on the Atlantis portal, rehearse the practical in the Practical NDT browser simulator, and do the hands-on work at an employer's own plant, shop or yard under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Longview. Certification comes from your employer once your hours, experience and exams are on file, not from the course itself.

Longview grew up on the East Texas Oil Field, and the industry that followed the oil boom never really left. A chemical complex on the Sabine River, a heavy equipment plant that builds machines for mines around the world, rail car shops, pipeline compressor stations and a crowd of fabrication and machine shops all sit within a short drive of downtown. Every one of them welds steel, runs pressure equipment or ships load-bearing parts, and every one of them needs people who can examine that work without cutting it apart.

We wrote this page for two kinds of reader. One is a Gregg County welder, helper or maintenance worker who wants to move into inspection, or a Level I technician who wants Level II without quitting a paying job. The other is a supervisor at a plant contractor, fabricator or equipment builder who has to qualify inspectors and show an auditor the paperwork behind each certificate. Both need training that a written practice can accept and that is taught by someone who has done the work in the field.

The instructor is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international field experience. Questions you post while you study reach him through the portal Q&A. To talk through your situation, send a Longview training enquiry; we reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Longview: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

East Texas inspection employers almost all use ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A as the basis of their certification programs. Because SNT-TC-1A is a recommendation rather than a law, each company publishes a written practice of its own that fixes the training hours, the experience hours, the examinations and the vision tests it applies. The usual route looks like this.

  1. Confirm you qualify. Check the recommended training and experience for your chosen method and make sure you can pass the near-vision and color tests your employer's written practice calls for. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker takes you through it.
  2. Choose a starting method. In Longview, visual inspection and ultrasonic thickness work on process piping are frequent first methods, with magnetic particle and penetrant testing close behind for welds and machined parts.
  3. Finish the formal training hours. Work through the Level I theory on the portal at your own pace. Access opens the moment you enrol and the course runs all year.
  4. Log supervised experience. Experience is recorded under a certified technician at your employer. It takes longer than the coursework and no course can stand in for it.
  5. Rehearse the practical. Run calibrations and indications in the Practical NDT simulator, then perform the hands-on practical on real parts at the employer's facility.
  6. Sit the general, specific and practical exams. Our Level III can administer them under your employer's written practice, or the employer's own Level III does.
  7. Be certified by the employer. The company signs the certification and keeps the record. Repeat the path for Level II and for every further method.

If you would rather hold a certificate that moves with you, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and the ASNT NDT Level III exams) is the alternative, and Atlantis prepares candidates for those exams as well.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Longview technicians

Each level is trained one method at a time. The table shows the methods we teach and where each one turns up around Longview.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Longview
Visual testing (VT)Lighting, viewing angles, weld profile gauges, acceptance criteria and reportingWeld fit-up and final checks in fabrication shops, plant turnaround walkdowns, structural steel
Ultrasonic testing (UT)Sound theory, thickness gauging, straight and angle beam, calibration blocks, DAC curvesWall loss on chemical plant piping and vessels, weld examination, pipeline integrity digs
Magnetic particle testing (MT)Magnetization methods, yokes and prods, wet and dry particles, demagnetizationWelds on heavy equipment frames, lifting gear, rail car components, carbon steel piping
Penetrant testing (PT)Visible and fluorescent penetrants, dwell times, developers, interpretationStainless and non-magnetic parts, machined components, weld root checks
Radiographic testing (RT)Radiation physics, exposure, film and digital image quality, interpretation (theory only)Pipeline and process weld radiography performed by licensed radiography firms

Start with NDT Level 1 training, move on with NDT Level 2 training, and when you are ready to run a program, look at ASNT Level III training. The published US fees on this page show what each package includes.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Longview

If one method pays its way in Longview, it is ultrasonic testing. A chemical site measures wall thickness at fixed monitoring locations year after year, and each reading has to be repeatable so the trend means something. Fabricators building pressure equipment and structural assemblies need angle beam weld examinations to code. Pipeline integrity crews confirm corrosion found by in-line tools when a section is dug up. A technician who calibrates properly, records clearly and knows when a reading looks wrong is useful in all three settings.

The ultrasonic testing training course starts with sound behavior in steel, transducer types and couplant, then thickness gauging and straight beam work, and builds to angle beam examination with distance amplitude correction. The simulator lets you repeat calibrations and scans until they feel routine before you touch a live component.

Magnetic particle testing comes next in local demand. Komatsu's wheel loaders, rail car underframes and lifting equipment are big welded carbon steel structures, and surface cracks at weld toes are what MT finds quickly.

Where NDT technicians work around Longview

NDT work in the Longview area comes from a handful of sectors rather than one dominant employer.

  • Chemical manufacturing. Eastman's Longview site is one of the largest chemical operations in the region. Plants like this run mechanical integrity programs that depend on thickness surveys, weld examination and turnaround inspection, much of it handled by contract inspection firms.
  • Heavy equipment. Komatsu builds large wheel loaders for mining at its Longview plant, the former LeTourneau works. Thick-section welding on frames and booms creates steady demand for VT, MT and UT.
  • Rail cars. Rail tank car building and repair has been part of Longview's economy for decades. Trinity announced in 2025 that one of its Longview facilities would close, so check current openings before counting on this sector.
  • Oil and gas. The East Texas Oil Field and the Haynesville gas play feed gathering lines, compressor stations and transmission pipelines across the region, which call on weld inspection during construction and integrity work afterwards.
  • Fabrication and machine shops. Smaller shops across Gregg, Harrison and Upshur counties build tanks, skids, structural steel and machined parts that often ship with NDT reports.

Most of these jobs are held by inspection service companies rather than by the plant owners themselves, which matters for certification: the contractor's written practice is the one that certifies you.

NDT schools and classes near Longview: what to compare

East Texas does not have a full-time NDT school, so most Longview candidates combine a local trade background with method training from elsewhere. Kilgore College, a few miles west, runs welding programs, and LeTourneau University in Longview teaches welding engineering. Both give a good grounding in welds and metallurgy, and graduates often move into inspection. The full-time NDT programs in Texas are further away, mostly around Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

When you compare any NDT course, ask these questions:

  • How many training hours does each method course give, and do they match what SNT-TC-1A recommends for the level?
  • Will your employer's written practice accept the training, and will the provider supply a record the employer can file?
  • Who runs the practical, on what parts, and does it happen at your employer's facility or somewhere you have to travel to?
  • Can you put questions to a Level III while you study, or are you left with recorded material only?
  • Does the course prepare you for ASNT central exams if you want a portable certificate later?

A self-paced theory course plus a practical at the employer suits people who already work in the trades and cannot give up shifts. A full-time program suits someone starting from scratch who can relocate for a while. Neither one certifies you on its own.

Online NDT training in Texas

Online theory works well across Texas because the distances are so long. A technician in Longview can study the same material as one in Midland or Corpus Christi, on the same portal, at whatever hour the shift pattern allows. What cannot move online is the hands-on part and the experience hours, which stay with the employer. Statewide options are summarized on the NDT training in Texas page, and the national picture is on NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Longview facility

Employers can have training delivered on-site at their own facility. Your technicians take theory on the portal, and the practical training and examinations run on your own components, gauges and procedures, which is usually what auditors want to see. If your company does not yet have a written practice, or the one you have no longer matches the work, our written practice development service and ASNT Level III consulting can set it up.

Where welding inspection is part of the job, Atlantis also runs a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course, delivered at the employer's facility, online, or one-to-one. AWS administers the exam and issues the certification.

Radiography licensing in Texas

Texas is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography is licensed by the Texas Department of State Health Services Radiation Control Program, which also certifies individual industrial radiographers. Completing RT theory training does not license or certify anyone to operate radiation sources. Radiography in Longview is carried out by licensed radiography companies. Atlantis teaches RT theory and interpretation and does not perform radiography in the US.

Practise before your practical exam

Most candidates who stumble on the practical do so on routine steps: an incomplete calibration, a missed reference reflector, a report that leaves out a required field. The Practical NDT simulator lets you repeat those steps in a browser until they come naturally, and the NDT practice tests check the written side for each method.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Longview

Is there an NDT school in Longview, Texas?

There is no full-time NDT school in Longview, and Atlantis NDT has no classroom here either. Local colleges teach welding and welding engineering, and NDT method training is usually taken online or through an employer, with the practical done on the employer's equipment.

How long does NDT training take?

The theory for one method at Level I can be finished in a few weeks of steady study. Certification takes longer because the supervised experience hours set by the written practice usually run to months for each method and level.

What does NDT training cost for Longview candidates?

You will find the published US fees for each course package in the table further up this page. Employer packages for a crew are quoted on request.

Can I train for NDT online in East Texas?

Yes. Theory is self-paced online on the Atlantis portal with Level III Q&A. The hands-on practical and experience hours are completed at an employer's facility.

Which NDT method should I start with in Longview?

Visual testing and ultrasonic thickness gauging are practical first steps for plant and pipeline work. If you come from a welding shop, magnetic particle testing is often a quick fit.

Are there NDT jobs near Longview?

Yes, mostly with inspection contractors serving chemical plants and pipelines, and with fabricators and equipment builders. Openings move with turnarounds and construction projects, so check current postings.

Does finishing a course make me a certified NDT technician?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after training, experience and exams are documented. ASNT central certification is the alternative if you want a certificate that does not depend on one employer.

Will my certification carry over if I change employers?

Employer certification ends when you leave that employer. A new employer can recertify you under its own written practice using your documented training and experience. ASNT 9712 certification stays with you.

Can I prepare for NDT Level III from Longview?

Yes. ASNT Level III training is self-paced online and prepares candidates for the ASNT NDT Level III Basic and method exams.

Can I take an API 510 or API 570 course through Atlantis?

No. Atlantis does not offer API inspector training. Many Longview plant inspectors hold API certificates through other providers, and our NDT method training sits alongside them.
